描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Boy with the Dragon", Qianlong, Qing dynasty, painted by Ai Qimeng, on silk with color, 228.5 cm long and 275 cm wide.　　Ai Qimeng was a Western missionary who came to China in 1745 and was summoned to the palace to paint for the Qianlong emperor. A total of nine works by Ai were included in the Shiqu Baoji, a collection book compiled by the Qing court. The painting level of Ai Qimeng was average compared to that of the Italian Lang Shining and the Frenchman Wang Zhicheng, but after the death of Lang Shining and Wang Zhicheng, Ai Qimeng became a European painter relied upon by the Qianlong Emperor.　　The painting is of a large horse of similar size to the real one, named "Baoji bay". In the lower right corner of the picture is a line signed: "Qianlong Kaishi in mid-autumn, Haixi minister Ai Qimeng painted". "At this time, the original chief European painter at the court, Lang Shining, died in 1766, and another European painter, Wang Zhicheng, passed away in 1768, so Ai Qimeng naturally became the most important painter. Therefore, Ai Qimeng naturally became the main painter who specialized in European painting style, so some of the tasks of depicting tribute objects were taken up by Ai Qimeng, such as this large banner of "Baoji bay".　　"Baoji bay" is the name of the horse in the painting. In June of 1771, the Mongolian Turks, who were nomadic in the lower Volga River in Russia, returned to their ancestral homeland in the East after nearly a year of bullying and oppression by the local Russians, led by their tribal leaders, the Wobashi and the Cebek Dolji (Wobashi's son-in-law). For this reason, Emperor Qianlong was very happy and received the chief of the tribe to appease and reward them. The horse named "Baoji bay" was a tribute presented to the Qianlong Emperor by Zebek Dorji at this time. This "Baoji bay" was painted by order of the Qianlong Emperor.　　If we talk about the painting skills alone, Ai Qimeng's painting is not much outstanding, and its painting level is much lower than that of Lang Shining, who is also a court painter. But after all, as a court painter, Ai Qimeng has played a documentary role with his brush, leaving us with a piece of history that once took place, and its value cannot be judged solely on the basis of the skill of his painting.
